parts:
Luxury ecommerce needs to decide what shopping agents can buy without asking. Repeat jewellery orders offer a starting point, with customer approval required above a chosen price threshold.

→ Shopify and Vercel have collaborated to let people and external AI agents shop a store, making purchase permissions a decision for retailers.

→ Kering Jewelry grew 12% in Q3 while group revenue stayed flat, giving luxury leaders reason to assess ecommerce opportunities by category.

→ Google Cloud added OpenAI models in private preview for enterprise customers, giving retail AI teams more model choice within one provider.

#ecommerce #luxury #retailtech
Spending permissions are becoming a merchandising decision for luxury ecommerce. Brands need to decide which purchases an AI agent can complete without another conversation with the customer.

Kering Jewelry grew 12% and Eyewear 6% year on year on a reported basis in Q3, while group revenue stayed flat. Those divisions give management reason to look beyond market conditions when assessing performance.

Shopify and Vercel are letting humans and external AI agents shop stores. Luxury retailers could test repeat jewellery orders with approval above a price threshold, comparing completed purchases with cancellations before expanding access.
Richemont is reportedly in talks to join a consortium bidding for De Beers Group, according to Jeweller. A successful bid would give the luxury group a direct interest in diamond mining.

Hermès posted 5.5% Q3 revenue growth, driven by Europe and the Americas. It kept its full-year forecast despite a deteriorating macroeconomic and geopolitical environment.
Walmart is rolling out controls that let shoppers oversee AI agent purchases and set spending limits. For retailers, this puts customer control over automated spending into the shopping experience.
Luk Fook’s revenue rose as diamond-jewellery demand improved. Its new London store gives the group its first European foothold as demand strengthens.

Anthropic launched Claude Duet to handle tasks while users are offline. For luxury retailers, required approval before sensitive actions such as payments puts a limit on what the agent can do unattended.
